input.title: Engine 2: local-pack declarations normalize themselves
input.head: claude/claudinite-issue-768-g2qga2
input.body:
The `local-pack-namespace` box of #768's Phase 1 — and the first change that actually rewrites a member's own file through the new machinery, so it is also the first real use of the release procedure #776 introduced.

## The gap this closes

`packs/basics/tasks/baselining/task.md` has carried this warning for a year:

> **Local-pack declaration normalization is currently unimplemented — do not assume it ran.**

Nothing rewrote a bare or legacy local-pack declaration to the canonical `local/<id>` token, because the `local-pack-namespace` record was written as *telemetry* for a rewrite step that lived in prose in a worker that has since been retired. Its `legacyPresent` probe could never reach zero, and its `retire: 'auto'` could never fire.

## What carries it now

**`normalizeLocalDeclarations`**, a named codemod in the registry. It is not a `rewrite` because the decision needs the repo's disk: `local_packs/<id>` → `local/<id>` is a pure pattern, but a **bare** id is a local pack only where that repo actually has one, and a bare id naming a canon pack must not be touched. No regex separates those. So the record declares one flag and the deterministic code ships with the engine — DESIGN §2.3's "rarely code", one op with one meaning rather than a general hatch for arbitrary code in a record.

It seeds nothing and drops nothing: entry objects keep their config, answers and order, only the id token changes, and a repo already on `local/` is a no-op.

**Regex rewrites** land alongside, since that is the shape §2.3 says engine migrations usually take. A pattern must be global — every replacement here means replace-all, and a non-global one would rewrite the first match and leave a half-migrated file that reads as migrated, so it throws rather than silently under-applying.

**One `applyMigration` for both appliers.** The standalone applier and the engine update flow each used to spell the op list themselves. That omission is silent — a record carrying a new op simply does nothing on the path that missed it — so there is now one runner, asserted by a test that pushes a record carrying every op through it.

## The release

The record moves to **version 2**, and `ENGINE_VERSION` with it: a member stamped at 1 fetches it again for exactly the reason the version gate exists. Per the procedure in `engine/RELEASES.md`, the bump is qualified by a canary rehearsal dispatched against this branch — [run 31633584458](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31633584458), green, against `6607b7c`, which is this tree; the only edit after it is the log row itself.

Worth noting that the machinery caught its own release: bumping the version turned `engine-release-record` red with *"this change releases engine version 2, and engine/RELEASES.md carries no row for it"*, and the live-selection test went red beside it. Both went green on the row.

## Fleet effect

This is the first record that changes member-owned content through the versioned path. On each member's next converge the declaration's local-pack tokens normalize to `local/<id>`; the engine accepts every form before and after (`packEntryId`'s strip is the permanent parser), so nothing can be stranded and a repo that never runs it stays correct.

## Verification

1495 tests green, `selftest --strict` green, work checks clean, world advisories identical to `origin/main` — plus the canary above, which is a real member repo converging against this branch with the new record in its gap.

Refs #768

Rollout plan for the versioned-updates design (`docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md`, PR #767). Each phase is independently landable and leaves the fleet working; baselining keeps running until Phase 5 removes it.

## Phase 0 — Version scaffolding (no behavior change) — landed in #769
- [x] Give the engine a version: a `VERSION` (or equivalent) stamped into the mount by the vendor set, advanced by release.
- [x] Give each canon pack a version number in its manifest.
- [x] Add `min_engine_version` to the pack manifest schema; validate shape only (no enforcement yet). *(landed as `minEngineVersion` — manifest vocabulary is camelCase; owner confirmed 2026-08-12)*
- [x] Extend the member stamp (`.claudinite-checks.json`) to record installed engine version and per-pack versions alongside the existing fields. The date stamp stays authoritative for now.
- [x] Move each existing migration record into its owning flow's home: engine migrations to the engine's `migrations/`, pack migrations to `packs/<pack>/migrations/`. The flat canon-wide `migrations/` directory retires with the split (DESIGN §3.7, owner decision 8).
- [x] Instrument `escalation()` so the fired `code` is countable across the fleet (dispatch issues already carry it; make it aggregatable). This validates the cost model before Phase 2 (DESIGN §7).

## Phase 1 — Engine releases and the engine update flow
- [x] Define an engine release: a tagged snapshot that has passed the live canary rehearsal once, at release time. *(owner decision 2026-08-12: a release is the **bump commit**, canary-gated — no tag; `engine/RELEASES.md` + the `engine-release-record` check, #776)*
- [x] Build the engine updater: clone the release's engine files into the mount wholesale, run engine migrations, converge the non-workflow wiring surfaces. *(#779 — `updates/engine-update.mjs`)*
  - [ ] …and enforce **no `agentic:` on an engine migration in the registry validator**. Deferred with Phase 4's note conversion: a validator that rejects records the canon itself still ships is broken on arrival. The flow already refuses them at `needs-human` (#779).
- [x] **Version-gate migration fetching in the vendoring flow** (owner decision 7): `compute-vendor-set` ships only the migration records above the repo's installed engine version, replacing the date-based recency window (`recordDirIsRecent`) as the fetch predicate. An up-to-date repo vendors none; a lagging repo vendors exactly its gap. *(#778)*
- [x] Rework `migrationActive()` legacy tolerance to be version-based in the same move ("tolerate the legacy shape while installed version < N"). *(#778 — same commit, as the constraint requires)*
- [ ] Gate auto-merge on `selftest --strict` of the converged tree; red → PR stays open + `need-human` label.
- [ ] Add the `force-merge-on-red-ci` per-invocation override (never a stored default).
- [ ] Define the **custom update** lane for the rare engine change that must touch `.github/workflows/` (MCP-credentialed session or human; explicitly named, never implicit).
- [x] Move the `local-pack-namespace` declaration rewrite (bare id → `local/<id>`) into a real engine migration — it is a regex on the declaration file, and it closes the long-open "unimplemented normalization" gap (baselining task.md §3). *(#781, released as engine 2; it needed a named codemod rather than a pure regex — a bare id is a local pack only where that repo has one)*

**Settled while building Phase 1**, so later phases inherit it rather than re-deciding it:
- A record declares `version` — the owning flow's version its change takes effect at — and lands with that bump. Which flow owns it stays structural (where the record lives).
- `migrationApplies` is the single predicate behind fetching *and* tolerance. In a member, "is this tolerated" reduces to "is it in my mount".
- Unknown installed version → the landed-date window, unchanged. Covers a fresh adoption, a repo that has not converged since versions existed, and the canon itself.
- One `applyMigration` runs every write op, for both the standalone applier and the engine flow — an op wired into one and not the other does nothing, silently.
- A record's write ops are declarative; where a decision needs the repo's disk it ships as a **named** codemod (`normalizeLocalDeclarations`), never a general code hatch.
- Phase 2's per-pack gate is the same predicate with the pack's number; nothing new to build for it.

## Phase 2 — Pack update flow
- [ ] Build the pack updater: vendor the new pack version, run its version-ranged migrations in order, converge wiring — **including `.github/workflows/`** (owner decision: workflow churn is the pack flow's; it lands through the MCP lane that baselining §2b uses today, which retires the withholding pattern).
- [ ] Apply the same version gate to per-pack migration fetching. *(the predicate already does this — what remains is the pack updater reading it)*
- [ ] Enforce `min_engine_version` before apply; violation → `need-human` terminal, never a guess.
- [ ] Implement the agentic apply stage: "apply the new pack rules — fix the repo, repair the tests," scoped to the update PR's branch.
- [ ] Re-home the executor-routine verification into this stage (the CCR routine is invisible to Actions; this is the only agent lane left).
- [ ] Uniform terminals: green → auto-merge per the repo's delivery setting; **any** non-green end (unanswered interview, red checks after repair, incomplete migration) → PR open + `need-human` + stop.

## Phase 3 — Install
- [ ] Install = the Phase 2 updater from a blank slate, **running no migrations** (owner decision 9): the vendored pack content is already the newest shape, so there is no older state to migrate — replaying history onto a fresh install is wasted work and a correctness hazard. The install fetches no migration records and stamps the pack's **latest** version directly.
- [ ] Add run-once-at-install seed ops (the "initial op": plain code the runner executes once — not a version migration). Mark them so no later update re-runs them; the seeded-vs-converged distinction is load-bearing (README badge row is the precedent).
- [ ] Route the adoption interview through the open-PR + `need-human` terminal; converge `adopt-pack` / `adopt-claudinite` onto this runner.

## Phase 4 — Cutover
- [ ] Convert the remaining `agentic:` notes → their owning pack's apply stage (or retire where already drained fleet-wide). **Now a precondition, not cleanup**: two engine records still carry notes (`pack-independence`, `prework-rename`), and the engine flow refuses to serve any repo whose gap contains one — see #779.
- [ ] Switch stamp authority from the date to installed versions; retire the held-stamp gating (#329/#330 semantics). *(fetching and tolerance already run on versions — what remains is note SELECTION)*

## Phase 5 — Retirement
- [ ] Remove `packs/basics/tasks/baselining/` (task.md, task.mjs, worker.mjs), its escalation codes, and its dispatch protocol, once every fleet member has updated through the new flows.
- [ ] Delete the `migrations/apply.mjs` + `migrations/registry.mjs` compatibility entry points (#769) — they exist only while a member's vendored worker can still invoke the old path.
- [ ] Drop the `agentic:` field from the migration schema.
- [ ] Vocabulary sweep: *baseline/baselining/rebaselining* → *update* across engine, packs, skills, docs (per `repo-text-sweeps`); rename the `adopt-claudinite` skill's baselining language; update sheepdog's `fleet-baseline` task name or note the exception.

## Ordering constraints
- Phase 1 before Phase 2: pack `min_engine_version` enforcement needs engine versions to exist; the version-gate + `migrationActive()` rework lands once, engine-side, and Phase 2 reuses it per pack.
- Phase 5 last, and only after fleet-wide adoption is verified (a member still on baselining must not lose its update path).
- The escalation-code measurement (Phase 0) should be read before committing Phase 2's scope — if `checks-not-green` dominates in practice, the agentic apply stage's budget deserves sizing to match.

## Risks
- **Skew during rollout**: while both mechanisms exist, a repo must be served by exactly one; gate by a per-repo flag in `.claudinite-checks.json`, flipped by the update that migrates it.
- **The regex-only discipline is a constraint on engine evolution**, accepted explicitly (DESIGN §2.3): a contract change that can't ship mechanically keeps backward compatibility or waits. Watch for pressure to route around it via "custom updates" — that lane is for workflows, not for contract changes.
- **Seed-op re-runs**: an install op that re-runs on update rewrites repo-owned surfaces (the README-diff class of bug). The run-once marking needs a conformance check of its own.
- **Tolerance/fetch coupling**: the version-gate must move fetching and `migrationActive()` together (one Phase 1 change, not two) — splitting them breaks legacy tolerance on lagging repos. *(done together in #778)*

content.text:
[#779](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/779) merged (`365a784`; rebased rather than merged, since the repo's `squash-merge-history` rule forbids merge commits on a work branch). Phase 1 is now six of eight boxes.

**[#781](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/781) — engine 2**, CI running. This closes the gap `task.md` has warned about for a year: *"Local-pack declaration normalization is currently unimplemented — do not assume it ran."* Nothing rewrote a bare or legacy local-pack declaration, because the record was telemetry for a rewrite step that lived in prose in a retired worker.

It needed more than the plan's "regex on the declaration file": `local_packs/<id>` → `local/<id>` is a pure pattern, but a **bare** id is a local pack only where that repo has one, and a bare id naming a canon pack must not be touched. So it ships as a named `normalizeLocalDeclarations` codemod — one op with one meaning, not a general code hatch — with regex rewrites added alongside for the cases that are pure patterns.

Both appliers now run one `applyMigration`; previously each spelled the op list itself, and an op wired into one and not the other does nothing at all on that path.

**The release procedure got its first real use, and caught its own release.** Bumping `ENGINE_VERSION` turned `engine-release-record` red — *"this change releases engine version 2, and engine/RELEASES.md carries no row for it"* — so I dispatched the canary against the branch, it converged a real member repo green ([run 31633584458](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31633584458)), and the row citing it turned the gate green.

This is the first record that changes member-owned content through the versioned path, so it's worth a careful read before merging.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#781](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/781) awaiting CI and your review. Remaining Phase 1: the `selftest --strict` auto-merge gate, `force-merge-on-red-ci`, and the named custom-update lane — all three are delivery-side, so they're the natural next unit together.
